item.title: US Equity Futures Climb as Crude Oil Price Dips: Markets Wrap
item.description: US stock futures advanced and crude oil retreated as traders weighed the latest geopolitical developments over Iran and looked ahead to a string of central bank rate decisions this week.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 26
item.description: Oil edged lower from a six-month high, even as US President Donald Trump signaled he was prepared to resume attacks on Iran.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Senegal Premier Raises Constitutional Option in Budget Standoff
item.description: Senegalese Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo said the government could use constitutional means to resolve a standoff over its 2026 budget if talks with lawmakers fail, as the dispute threatens to complicate efforts to secure a new International Monetary Fund program.
item.dc:creator: Katarina Höije

item.title: BYD’s Korea Expansion Challenges Hyundai Dominance on Home Turf
item.description: When Lee Seongdong decided to replace his 2016 Chevrolet Spark in April, a two-year wait for Hyundai Motor Co.’s Casper Electric was already pushing him toward BYD Co.’s Dolphin. He was so impressed by the feature-rich ride that he signed a contract on the spot.
item.dc:creator: Hyonhee Shin and Andy Lin

item.title: De olho nas eleições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula chegam ao segundo turno tecnicamente empatados após debate e atos realizados no país nesta sábado. Com reportagem e edição de Patricia Xavier e produção de Beatriz Amat e Fabiola Moura. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 9 Days to Midterm Elections, Big Tech Earnings
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by MetLife Investment Management Chief Market Strategist Drew Matus, Financial Times Associate Editor and “Sea Change” Author Rana Foroohar, Former Prime Minister of Israel Ehud Olmert, Texas Rep. Dan Crenshaw, Former US Ambassador to Israel Daniel Shapiro, CBS News, White House & Political Correspondent Ed O’Keefe and Puck Washington Author Abby Livingston. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inside The Two Argentinas Under Javier Milei
item.description: President Javier Milei has brought inflation down and opened Argentina to more investment, helping fuel a boom in energy and other export industries. But manufacturing, retail and small businesses are struggling, leaving many Argentines feeling that the recovery is passing them by. One year before the election, Milei’s biggest test may be unifying an increasingly fragmented economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zero-Day Option Traders Are Betting Against Big S&P 500 Swings
item.description: While some investors position for AI earnings, geopolitics and interest rates to send stocks either to new highs or into a tailspin, zero-day option traders have increasingly bet that the S&P 500 Index will remain calm.
item.dc:creator: Christian Dass

item.title: Halloween Candy Prices Reflect Cocoa’s Wild Ride
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Ignacio Canalas Polo explains why chocolate and Halloween candy remain expensive even after cocoa prices retreated from their peaks, pointing to persistent supply pressures in Ivory Coast and Ghana and manufacturers’ efforts to manage costs. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Polo says consumers may see more promotions, but structurally higher cocoa costs and product reformulation mean chocolate prices are unlikely to return quickly to previous levels. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Looks Set to Pause After September Rate Hike
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News Federal Reserve reporter Maria Eloisa Capurro previews the Fed’s upcoming rate decision, with policymakers widely expected to pause after September’s first rate increase since 2023 despite inflation remaining above target. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Capurro explains why investors will scrutinize Chair Kevin Warsh’s language for clues about another potential rate increase and his efforts to reshape how the central bank approaches monetary policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rubio Plans Trilateral Negotiations Over Ukraine, Johnson Says
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson says he has spoken over the weekend to President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who told him the US is planning trilateral negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Sam Kim

item.title: Emerging Debt Outruns Treasuries as Rich-World Fiscal Fears Grow
item.description: Investors from JPMorgan Asset Management to Generali and Ninety One SA are loading up on emerging-market debt, defying a surge in Treasury yields that would once have sent them running for the exits.
item.dc:creator: Heng Xie and Selcuk Gokoluk

item.title: What’s Happening in EM: Bond Investors Turn to Developing World
item.description: This week, Mpho Hlakudi and Selcuk Gokoluk discuss how some of the world’s biggest asset managers increase their exposure to emerging markets despite the surge in US Treasury yields, weakening a traditional correlation in financial markets.
item.dc:creator: Selcuk Gokoluk

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: The artist behind the moving bird in the Kelly Clarkson/Toy Store drama, colleges helping grads pay loans back, child-free flights and cruises, and a 'timeless ticket' to the World Series: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IndiGo, Air India to Shift Some Flights to New Mumbai Airport
item.description: IndiGo and Air India will move some of their international operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport as two of India’s biggest airlines expand their presence at the new aviation facility serving the country’s financial capital.
item.dc:creator: P R Sanjai and Siddhi Nayak

item.title: French Bond Rout Puts Crisis at Heart of ECB Succession Endgame
item.description: The European Central Bank’s presidency race looks increasingly likely to hinge on which candidate can best take on the bond vigilantes.
item.dc:creator: Mark Schroers and Craig Stirling

item.title: Brookfield to Open Doha Office to Deepen Middle East Reach
item.description: Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. is opening an office in Qatar, deepening its presence in the Middle East where many countries are grappling with the economic fallout from the war.
item.dc:creator: Adveith Nair

item.title: Goldman Cuts Kospi 12-Month Target by 25% as AI Trade Unravels
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. strategists slashed their target for South Korea’s Kospi Index by 25%, after raising it repeatedly this year, as concerns over the artificial intelligence trade intensify.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Vishnoi

item.title: BC Left-Wing Leader Loses to Conservatives in Vote He Called
item.description: British Columbia elected its first Conservative Party majority in 98 years, swinging Canada’s third most populous province to the political right.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Seal

item.title: Brazil Election: Lula Rallies Supporters for One Last Comeback
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wasn’t going down without a fight. And his fans weren’t ready to give up on him. Here, marching down Sao Paulo’s most iconic avenue, they were bearing witness to what may turn out to be the last rally by the most defining figure of Latin America’s left.
item.dc:creator: Augusta Saraiva and Andrew Rosati
